html:
Tlaxcala, or Tlaxcallan, was a Nahua state in the highlands of central Mexico, east of the Valley of Mexico, that stayed independent of the Aztecs and then became the key ally of the Spanish in their conquest.

It was a confederation of four altepetl, or city-states, ruled jointly by their lords with a council, which is why Spanish writers called it a republic. It was surrounded by lands of the Aztec Triple Alliance, which never conquered it. The two sides fought ritual "flower wars" to take captives for sacrifice, and the Aztecs cut Tlaxcala off from trade, so it lacked salt and cotton. Its neighbour Cholula often sided with the Aztecs. Otomí soldiers guarded its borders.

When Hernán Cortés marched inland in 1519, the Tlaxcalans fought him first, then made an alliance. They saw a chance to destroy their old enemy. Tlaxcalan warriors joined the massacre at Cholula, sheltered the Spanish after their flight from Tenochtitlan in 1520, and supplied thousands of fighters and porters for the fall of Tenochtitlan in 1521.

In return the Spanish crown gave Tlaxcala special privileges, such as freedom from encomienda grants. Tlaxcalan families were later sent north to found towns among the Guachichiles and other Chichimec peoples, to help end the long Chichimeca War. In modern Mexico, Tlaxcala is the smallest state.
sum: Tlaxcala, or Tlaxcallan, was a Nahua state in the highlands of central Mexico, east of the Valley of Mexico, that stayed independent of the Aztecs and then became the key ally of the Spanish in their conquest.
